title: arXiv Trending Math — Thursday, 5 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. The ordering is inferred from mathematical claims and scope rather than measured popularity; citation evidence for papers this recent is limited. This is a notable-recent-papers ranking, not a popularity ranking.

sections.title: Polylogarithmic bound for the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture
sections.abstract: For graphs excluding a fixed forest as an induced subgraph and with bounded clique number, the authors improve the known subpolynomial chromatic-number bound to a polylogarithmic one.
sections.claimed_result: For every fixed tree T and positive integer k, every finite T-induced-free graph G with clique number at most k and at least two vertices satisfies χ(G) ≤ C_{T,k}(log |G|)^{14k} (arXiv introduction, Theorem 1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: T and k are fixed; G is finite, contains no induced copy of T, and has clique number at most k.
sections.unique_caveat: The result improves the asymptotic bound but does not establish the conjectured chromatic bound independent of graph size.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The introduction states an explicit improvement over the recent |G|^{o(1)} bound; this is the strongest explicit bound improvement in the selected batch.

sections.title: Uniqueness of the hexagonal lattice's universal optimality
sections.abstract: Building on a recent proof of universal optimality, the authors show that the planar hexagonal lattice is the only periodic point configuration with that property, up to Euclidean motion.
sections.claimed_result: For every periodic C ⊂ R² of density one, the hexagonal lattice minimizes every Gaussian energy, and equality for even one Gaussian parameter implies congruence to the hexagonal lattice (arXiv HTML, Theorem 1.2).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Periodic configurations in the plane at density one; uniqueness is up to Euclidean motion. The paper also treats nonzero completely monotone potentials when the reference energy is finite.
sections.unique_caveat: Uniqueness is deliberately restricted to periodic configurations; deleting finitely many lattice points gives noncongruent configurations with unchanged density and limiting energy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Adds a uniqueness theorem to recent universal optimality and treats every periodic configuration at fixed density, not just lattices; potential extension covers completely monotone potentials under finite-energy conditions.

sections.title: Proof of two conjectures on the log-concavity of partition ranks and cranks
sections.abstract: The authors prove two conjectures asserting log-concavity of the partition-crank and partition-rank counting sequences over specified ranges of the statistic.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove A_k(m,n)^2 > A_k(m−1,n)A_k(m+1,n) for k∈{1,2}, n≥72, and |m|≤n−k−71, where A_1=M is the crank count and A_2=N the rank count (arXiv HTML, Theorem 1.3).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Integer partition size n and statistic index m in the stated ranges; the rank case starts at n≥73 because of the range condition.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem covers the conjectured ranges, not every boundary value in the full support of each rank or crank sequence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Proves two named conjectures and obtains strict log-concavity for two classical partition statistics; cross-listed in combinatorics and number theory.

sections.title: On Diameter Graphs Problems: A proof of Brass's Conjecture
sections.abstract: For diameter graphs of finite point sets in three-dimensional space, the authors prove Brass's conjecture by showing that removing at most one point suffices to make the remaining graph 3-colorable.
sections.claimed_result: For every finite S ⊂ R³, deleting at most one vertex from its diameter graph leaves a 3-colorable induced subgraph; the paper also answers a question of Dol'nikov (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite point sets in R³; adjacency means two points are at distance equal to the diameter of the set.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is the specific three-dimensional, three-color case and does not settle the analogous question for arbitrary dimension and color number.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims a resolution of a named conjecture with the explicit bound of one deleted point; cross-listed in combinatorics and metric geometry.

sections.title: Certified Collision Exclusion and an Unconditional Upper Bound Λ<0.156821 for the de Bruijn--Newman Constant
sections.abstract: The authors describe a computer-assisted collision-exclusion proof yielding the unconditional bound Λ < 0.156821 in the Polymath normalization.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim Λ < 156821/10^6, combining a finite-height verification with a continuation argument, certified exclusions, and a uniform barrier at infinity (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The normalization is that of Polymath; the conclusion concerns the transition parameter beyond which all zeros of the heat-deformed Riemann xi-function are real.
sections.unique_caveat: This computer-assisted preprint claim depends on the certificate and its proof-to-computation interface; neither was independently verified here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: States a specific unconditional bound for a constant tied to the Riemann xi-function and describes a finite certificate with 44,182 torus boxes and separator data.

sections.title: Gaussian free field limit for the Airy_β line ensemble
sections.abstract: For every β>0, the authors prove that a rescaled centered height function of the Airy_β line ensemble converges to the Gaussian free field in the half-plane.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim convergence of the centered Airy_β height function to the half-plane Gaussian free field, with spatial coordinate x ↦ √(-x) and β entering through a √β field rescaling (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: For each fixed β>0 under the paper's specified space-time and field rescalings.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not specify the precise mode of convergence; the theorem's topology and test-function assumptions must be checked before applying the limit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The limit holds for every positive β and links random line ensembles to a two-dimensional field; cross-listed in probability and mathematical physics.

sections.title: Almost All 3-uniform Hypergraphs are Class 1
sections.abstract: For a stated range of edge probabilities, a random 3-uniform binomial hypergraph has chromatic index equal to its maximum degree with high probability, with contrasting results for higher uniformities.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim H ~ H^{(3)}_{n,p} is Class 1 with high probability when n^{-2/3-1/200} ≤ p ≤ 0.99, and state non-Class-1 results for a broad range when k≥4 and k does not divide n (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Random binomial k-uniform hypergraph; the 3-uniform assertion has the explicit probability interval above; the higher-uniformity contrast is restricted as stated by the authors.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is asymptotic and probabilistic; it does not assert that every 3-uniform hypergraph in the range is Class 1.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Extends an almost-everywhere Class 1 result from random graphs to 3-uniform random hypergraphs and identifies a contrasting obstruction at higher uniformities; cross-listed with discrete mathematics.

sections.title: Matching Random Point Sets with Minimum Distortion
sections.abstract: For two independent uniform samples of n points from [0,1], the authors show that the typical minimum distortion of a bijection is n^{2/3} up to polylogarithmic factors.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim distortion n^{2/3} up to polylogarithmic factors with high probability for two independent uniform samples from [0,1], with a multiscale construction for the upper bound (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two independent n-point samples from [0,1] equipped with uniform measure; distortion is measured for a bijection between induced finite metric spaces.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated exponent is established for this one-dimensional uniform model, not arbitrary metric-measure spaces.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Gives upper and lower bound mechanisms for a nontrivial distortion exponent and spans probability, combinatorics, and metric geometry.

sections.title: Uniqueness of Ricci flows from singular initial data
sections.abstract: The authors establish uniqueness for Ricci flows with nonnegative sectional curvature and scaling-invariant curvature bounds when induced distances converge, up to isometry, to the same initial distance function.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim uniqueness under nonnegative sectional curvature and scaling-invariant curvature bounds when induced distance functions converge to the same initial metric up to isometry; a compact-case variant is also stated (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The main statement assumes nonnegative sectional curvature, scaling-invariant curvature bounds, and convergence of distance functions to a common initial distance function up to isometry.
sections.unique_caveat: The compact-case extension is described only as requiring a restricted singular-set size and suitable weaker conditions in the abstract; the precise conditions require the paper text.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Addresses uniqueness from singular initial data and cross-lists differential geometry with analysis of PDEs; its hypotheses make a precise claim in a geometric-flow setting.
